description: Shared MySQL / MariaDB contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server. The MySQL collector (#488 / PR #88) shipped WITHOUT a fixture; issue #107 (Galera wsrep cluster state) adds this one and it becomes the source of truth, vendored byte-identical server-side. Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/mysql_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_mysql.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip with ONLY the PyMySQL driver mocked (up to agent 1.24.0 the collector shelled out to the mysql CLI and these inputs were its stdout) -- each scenario's 'results' are the rows the driver returns per statement (keyed by the exact SQL; values are fed back as the bytes PyMySQL hands the collector), a scenario's 'connect_error' is the OSError behind a failed connection to the default socket /run/mysqld/mysqld.sock, and mysql_metrics(**config) must equal scenario['payload']. The server's spec/requests/api_collect_mysql_spec.rb posts scenario['payload'] under data['mysql'] through /collect and asserts Ingesters::Mysql ingests each shape (Galera present / absent / unreachable envelope). 'config', 'results' and 'connect_error' are agent-side inputs the server ignores. The payloads did not change with the move to the driver, except the wording of error_detail (free text: the server stores and shows it, never parses it) and the new 'galera' flag (see galera_contract). Change the payload shape only in lockstep across both repos, keeping the two copies byte-identical.
_agent_min_version_note: MINOR bump: Galera adds a new user-facing capability (cluster-state gauges + the server-side galera_cluster_degraded trigger). Released main is 1.13.1; the only PRs pushed above it are 1.14.0 (Docker image-inventory #102) and 1.14.1 (TSDB #103), so 1.15.0 is the next free minor. MySQL has NO server version gate (no FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS entry -- it is purely config-driven, mysql_enabled defaults false), so nothing gates on this number; it exists only to date the payload.
galera_contract: The Galera keys are the whitelisted subset of SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'wsrep%', merged into the SAME data['mysql'] object as the base metrics (no new payload object, no new config). Galera detection: the agent reads the global wsrep_on variable with max_connections/version and sends the wsrep statement only when it is ON; otherwise every wsrep_* key is simply ABSENT (no-data server-side, not null). A plain MariaDB answers the wsrep statement too (see scenario mariadb_without_galera): agents up to 1.24.0 shipped its 'Disconnected' cluster of size 0, which the server must not read as a degraded cluster. The reachable payload therefore carries 'galera' (agent 1.24.1+): true on a Galera node, false otherwise; ABSENT when the variables could not be read (unknown, like an older agent). The server clears any Galera state it stored for the host on galera false (a plain MariaDB an older agent reported), and keeps it on galera true without wsrep_* keys (a Galera node whose wsrep statement failed this tick) and when the key is absent. The galera_healthy and galera_degraded payloads were checked against a real 3-node MariaDB 11.8.9 cluster (healthy; then two nodes SIGKILLed: non-Primary, size 1, local state 0/Initialized, ready OFF, connected ON). The keys are likewise ABSENT when the reachability envelope reports unreachable/config_error -- the probe fails before the wsrep statement runs, so the payload is envelope-only. Never fabricate: a wsrep_* numeric that fails to parse (NULL / garbage), a non-finite float (inf/nan/overflow -- these would serialize as invalid Infinity/NaN JSON and poison the whole tick), and a present-but-blank status string are all OMITTED, not sent as null or empty. Every shipped float is therefore finite. All values are instantaneous gauges/status -- nothing to rate; ints/floats are parsed to native types, non-blank status strings ship verbatim. Same absent-vs-null discipline as the rest of the reachable/error envelope from #488.

field_contract._base: reachable/connections/queries/slow_queries/aborted_connects/uptime/innodb_buffer_pool_hit_ratio/innodb_buffer_pool_usage_pct/max_connections/version/is_replica/replication are the pre-#107 MySQL payload (PR #88); unchanged here and included so the round-trip pins the WHOLE data['mysql'] object, not just the Galera delta.
field_contract.galera: Whether the server is a Galera node: its global wsrep_on variable read ON (bool, agent 1.24.1+). false = not a Galera node: clear any stored Galera state. Absent = the variables could not be read, or an older agent: unknown, keep what is stored. Never present on the unreachable envelope.
field_contract.wsrep_cluster_size: wsrep_cluster_size -- number of nodes in the component this node sees (int). A drop below the configured size is the split-brain / lost-quorum signal.
field_contract.wsrep_cluster_status: wsrep_cluster_status verbatim -- 'Primary' when the node is in the primary component; anything else ('non-Primary', 'Disconnected') means it cannot serve writes. Drives galera_cluster_degraded server-side.
field_contract.wsrep_local_state: wsrep_local_state -- numeric node FSM state (int; 4 == Synced). Pairs with wsrep_local_state_comment.
field_contract.wsrep_local_state_comment: wsrep_local_state_comment verbatim -- human label for wsrep_local_state ('Synced', 'Donor/Desynced', 'Joining', 'Initialized').
field_contract.wsrep_ready: wsrep_ready verbatim -- 'ON' when the node will accept queries, 'OFF' when it will reject them.
field_contract.wsrep_connected: wsrep_connected verbatim -- 'ON' when the node has network connectivity to the cluster.
field_contract.wsrep_flow_control_paused: wsrep_flow_control_paused -- fraction of time (0.0-1.0) replication was paused by flow control since the last status read (float). Sustained > 0 means a slow node is throttling the cluster.
field_contract.wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg: wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg -- average length of the local received-write-set queue (float). > 0 means this node is falling behind on apply.
field_contract._dropped: Every other wsrep_* row (wsrep_provider_name, wsrep_protocol_version, wsrep_local_state_uuid, ...) is NOT ingested and is dropped from the payload; only the eight keys above are whitelisted.

galera_healthy.description: A healthy 3-node Galera / MariaDB member: Primary component, local state 4/Synced, ready+connected ON, negligible flow control. Pins native typing (cluster_size/local_state ints, flow_control_paused/local_recv_queue_avg floats, status strings verbatim) and the whitelist drop of the extra wsrep rows (wsrep_protocol_version, wsrep_provider_name).

galera_degraded.description: A partitioned Galera node cut off from quorum: non-Primary component, cluster_size collapsed to 1, local state 0/Initialized, wsrep_ready OFF (rejects queries), heavy flow-control pausing and a backed-up recv queue. This is the shape that fires galera_cluster_degraded server-side. reachable stays true -- the node is up, the CLUSTER is degraded.

non_galera.description: A plain (non-Galera) MySQL 8 server. MySQL has no wsrep_on variable, so the wsrep statement is not even sent and no wsrep_* key is emitted (no-data == not clustered). The payload is exactly the pre-#107 base object; the server sees no Galera keys and treats the host as non-clustered.

mariadb_without_galera.description: A plain MariaDB with no Galera (wsrep_on OFF, wsrep_provider none: the default install). MariaDB 10.1+ is built with wsrep and answers SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'wsrep%' all the same -- the 17 rows below were MEASURED on 10.11.19 (11.8.9 answers the same, wsrep_cluster_conf_id -1) -- with wsrep_cluster_status 'Disconnected', wsrep_ready 'OFF' and wsrep_cluster_size 0, which agents up to 1.24.0 shipped and the server read as a degraded Galera cluster. The agent now reads wsrep_on with the variables and sends the wsrep statement only when it is ON, so no wsrep_* key is emitted. Servers must clear stored Galera state on a reachable payload that carries `version` (the variables, wsrep_on included, were read) and no wsrep_* key: that server is not a Galera node -- keeping the last stored values, as an absent key otherwise means, would keep the 'Disconnected' cluster older agents stored for every plain MariaDB forever. Servers still receiving those keys from older agents can tell them apart: exactly wsrep_cluster_size 0, wsrep_cluster_status, wsrep_ready and wsrep_connected, with NO wsrep_local_state -- the provider's own status, present on every Galera node (MEASURED on a 3-node MariaDB 11.8.9 cluster, synced, joining and without quorum); a size of 0 alone proves nothing, since a joining Galera node reports it too.

unreachable.description: The connection to the server's socket is refused (a socket left by a crashed server), so mysql_metrics returns the envelope only and never runs the wsrep statement. Proves the Galera keys are absent on unreachable -- the server must not read (or fabricate) cluster state from a host it could not reach.

payload.error_detail: ERROR 2002: Can't connect to local MySQL server through socket '/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock' (Connection refused)
